last_checked.note: 2026-07-30 check: v6.0.0.24 (released 2026-07-28T18:46:17Z) vs prior v6.0.0.21. Normalized error/warn/info/critical rates per hour-in-production are flat vs. the prior run (e.g. error/hr ~3176 then vs ~3400 now) -- the raw totals look like a jump but reflect ~52h of production time this run vs ~21h last run, not a regression. Rollout confirmed broad and healthy: 19 clusters via cluster_name aggregate (production-aws-us1a/us2a/eu5a/ap1a, staging x2, sandbox x2, plus 9 customer-dedicated MPC/GCP clusters: flywire, ippen, komgo, cargosense, preset, wealthsimple, beam, koa, zeta, hmetrix). This resolves the open question from the 07-23 note about clusters shrinking from 6 to 4 -- that was a sampling artifact of the raw events/search page limit (100), not a real rollout regression. Used /api/v2/logs/analytics/aggregate (group_by status, group_by cluster_name) for accurate full-window counts since /events/search truncates to page limit. Added ~11 new low-volume (1-22 occurrence) benign patterns to known_noise: generic exception wrappers (HTTPException/SupersetErrorException), CSP-not-configured config warning, RBAC permission-denied notices, slack_sdk/pkg_resources deprecation UserWarnings, report-scheduler overlap guards, and a SQL-redaction log line. Deliberately did NOT suppress two new patterns, left them open for next-run comparison: (1) a single 'error'-status Snowflake session error on prs_partnership_saos (customer table, prs_ prefix) -- 'Cannot perform SELECT, session has no current database' -- looks like an isolated customer-side Snowflake session issue, not a superset-shell regression, but only one data point so far; (2) Slack 'not_allowed_token_type' / missing channels:read scope errors on report notifications -- customer Slack app config gaps, tied to the v1 Slack API removal called out for Superset 6.0.0 (we are now on v6.0.0.24) -- worth checking if usage climbs as more customers hit the removal. Also saw one odd internal-sounding message 'dashboard capture proceeding with zero chart holders -- readiness gate inactive' (1 occurrence) that doesn't match standard OSS Superset wording; not enough volume to investigate now but flagged for awareness.
